## Research Interests

**Environmental Economics · Urban Economics · Spatial Economics · Applied Microeconomics**

My research examines how environmental risks and natural disasters affect housing markets, households, and local economic outcomes. I use spatial, administrative, environmental, economic, and other high-resolution data to study how environmental shocks and information about environmental risks are reflected in economic decisions and outcomes.

---

## Working Papers

### Dissertation Papers

#### Water Contamination and Real Estate Prices: Evidence from Hawaii's Red Hill Fuel Leak

This paper examines how information about environmental contamination risk affects housing markets, using the Red Hill fuel leak in Hawaiʻi as a setting to study the capitalization of environmental risk into residential property values.

**[Job Market Paper]** · **[PDF]** · **[Slides]**

#### Volcanic Eruption and Real Estate Prices: Impact of the 2018 Kīlauea Eruption

This paper examines the impact of the 2018 Kīlauea eruption on real estate prices.

**[PDF]** · **[Slides]**

#### Natural Disasters and Financial Outcomes: Evidence from Multiple US Disasters

This paper examines the relationship between natural disasters and financial outcomes using evidence from multiple disasters in the United States.

**[PDF]**

### Other Papers

#### The Impact of Natural Disasters on Mental Health: Evidence from the United States

This paper examines the effects of natural disasters on mental health outcomes in the United States.
